video.label: Blast Motion - Youth Hitting Drills - Swing Plane

extraction.verifiedTitle: Blast Motion PVC Pipe On-Plane Drill
extraction.overallNotes: Demonstrates a PVC pipe drill where a youth hitter holds a pipe across the chest to learn how torso rotation and body posture create the swing plane across different tee locations, avoiding lunging or diving at the ball.

claims.claimText: Hitters should adjust swing plane to different pitch locations through torso rotation and body posture rather than diving their chest forward toward the ball.
claims.sourceProposition: Hitters must rotate the torso to bring the pipe around to the tee, avoiding diving the chest forward at the ball.
claims.observableEvidence: Maintaining spinal posture during torso rotation with the pipe making contact with the tee without forward chest lunging.
claims.appliesWhen: Working on swing plane control, torso rotation, and pitch location adjustment.
claims.doesNotApplyWhen: Full game situations where timing and stride dynamics vary unpredictably.
claims.qualityNotes: Uses a task-based constraint drill with a PVC pipe across the chest to foster rotational posture control.
claims.causeVsSymptomNote: Diving at the ball is identified as a mechanical flaw caused by attempting to reach the pitch with the chest rather than rotating properly.
claims.coachingCue: Rotate around your center so the pipe comes to the tee—don't dive your chest forward.
claims.levelScopeNote: Appropriate for youth through advanced hitters as a posture and rotation isolation drill.

drills.name: PVC Pipe Chest Rotation Drill
drills.targetedProblem: Lunging/diving at the ball with the upper body and failing to use body posture to control swing plane.

weakOrRejectedNotes: General mention of Blast Motion 'on-plane metric' omitted as a biomechanical claim since it relies on proprietary sensor software, though the underlying mechanical drill is fully captured.
